answer: An agent market can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards. Repeated identities then require repeated deposits, while slashing a stake for provable fraud makes each attempt costly; reputation can accrue only to the same locked account, so splitting activity across fresh names does not multiply trust. The jetty of admission is narrow: a vertex must bridge its stake to an accountable history, and an attacker pays capital and risks losing it for every Sybil.
